CHAPTER IV
PROTECTION OF WOMEN
Part One
General

Third Part
Prevention of Violence Against Women

Paragraph 1
General

Article 34
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women for the following year.
(3) The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 33
(1) The Regent conducts monitoring of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women.
(2) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of women in the Region.
(3) The monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) is conducted periodically on PD through the Agency.
(4) The monitoring is conducted from planning up to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of women for the current year.

Part Four

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency of North Central Timor. 2. Regional Government is the Government of North Central Timor Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of North Central Timor. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of North Central Timor Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of North Central Timor Regency. 6. Office is the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and Child Protection. 7. Head of Office is the Head of Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment. 8. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus in North Central Timor Regency. 9. Head of Regional Apparatus is the Head of Regional Apparatus in North Central Timor Regency. 10. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of development planning and regional research. 11. Head of Agency is the Head of the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of planning. 12. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities. 13. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of regional development policies and programs. 14. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of social construction and can change due to social and cultural circumstances of society. 15. Gender Equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so they are able to play a role and participate in the development process. 16. Gender Justice is a process to be fair to men and women. 17. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 18. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point, hereinafter referred to as Focal Point PUG is a PD apparatus that has the ability to conduct gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 19. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMD is the elaboration of the vision, mission and program of the Regent whose preparation is guided by the Regional Long-Term Development Plan, which contains regional development strategies, general regional policies, 3 regional programs and macroeconomic framework that includes an overview of the economy as a whole including the direction of fiscal policy in a work plan in the form of a regulatory framework and funding framework that is indicative. 20. Gender Analysis is a process built systematically to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in development and the benefits they enjoy. 21. Gender Responsive Budget is a performance-based budget allocation for certain programs or activities whose input, output, and outcome indicators can guarantee the fulfillment of the aspirations and needs of women and men fairly. 22. Communication, Information and Education hereinafter abbreviated as KIE is the delivery of messages in the form of information, ideas or facts related to gender mainstreaming that need to be known by the community directly or indirectly through communication channels to message recipients to obtain effects, as a process of behavioral change towards gender responsiveness. 23. Village/Sub-district Development Planning Deliberation hereinafter referred to as Musrembangkel is an annual village/sub-district development planning deliberation forum that involves development actors in the Village/Sub-district. 24. Sub-district Development Planning Deliberation hereinafter referred to as Musrembangcam is a deliberation forum among development actors to discuss and agree on steps to handle priority program activities listed in the list of proposed village development planning activities that are integrated with development priorities of the North Central Timor Regency in the sub-district area coordinated by the Regional Development Planning Agency and implemented by the Sub-district Head. 25. Development planning deliberation for the preparation of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as Musrembang RPJMD is a deliberation forum among stakeholders to discuss, sharpen and agree on the draft Regional Medium-Term Development Plan. 26. Strategic Plan hereinafter referred to as Renstra is a five-year planning document that contains the vision, mission, objectives, strategies, policies, programs and development activities in accordance with the organizational tasks and functions as an elaboration of the RPJMD. 27. Work Plan hereinafter referred to as Renja is a one-year planning document that contains policies, programs, and development activities both planned directly by the Regional Apparatus and pursued by encouraging community participation as an elaboration of the Renstra. 28. Regional Government Work Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RKPD is a one-year planning document that contains policies, programs, and development activities both planned directly by the Regional Government and pursued by encouraging community participation as an elaboration of the Renstra. 29. Regional Action Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RAD is an activity planning document prepared by a technical team to be implemented in a certain period/time. 30.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.
In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.
The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs, through data on Civil Servants based on gender available in the field.
Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.
In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.
The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs, through data on Civil Servants based on gender available in the field.
Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.
In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.
The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs, through data on Civil Servants based on gender available in the field.
Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.
In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.
The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs, through data on Civil Servants based on gender available in the field.
Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.
In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.
The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs, through data on Civil Servants based on gender available in the field.
Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.
In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.
The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs, through data on Civil Servants based on gender available in the field.
Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.
In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.
The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs, through data on Civil Servants based on gender available in the field.
Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.
In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.
The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs, through data on Civil Servants based on gender available in the field.
Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.
